For $X=OF(M,\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal{F}=\widetilde{\mathcal O}$, let $\kappa:X\to B$ be the fibre bundle of Theorem~\ref{thm:mol} and let $\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}:X\to W$ be the basic fibre bundle. The two maps have the same fibres. Hence Lemma~\ref{lem:same-fibres-diffeo} gives a unique diffeomorphism
\[
\Phi:B\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }W
\]
such that $\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}=\Phi\circ\kappa$. In what follows, whenever this setting is fixed, we identify $B$ and $W$ through this diffeomorphism and regard $A=b(X,\mathcal{F})$ as a Lie algebroid over $B$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:mol}, the fibres of $\kappa$ are the closures of the leaves of $\mathcal{F}$. By \cite{MoerdijkMrcun:IFLG}*{Corollary~4.25}, the leaves of the basic foliation $\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{bas}}$ are also the closures of the leaves of $\mathcal{F}$. Since $\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}$ is the quotient map by $\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{bas}}$, its fibres are the leaves of $\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{bas}}$. Thus $\kappa$ and $\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}$ have the same fibres, and the conclusion follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:same-fibres-diffeo}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
\label{def:mc}
Recall that a $\mathfrak g$-valued $1$-form $\eta$ is a Maurer--Cartan form if $d\eta+\frac12[\eta,\eta]=0$.
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
If $(L,\mathcal F)$ is transversely parallelizable on a compact connected manifold and all basic functions on $(L,\mathcal F)$ are constant, then the evaluation maps $\operatorname{ev}_x \colon l(L,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }N_x(\mathcal F)$ are isomorphisms, and the associated canonical Maurer--Cartan form is $(\omega_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi):=\operatorname{ev}_x^{-1}(\operatorname{pr}_x^N(\xi))$.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:MC-naturality}
Let $(L_b,\mathcal F_b)$ and $(L_{b'},\mathcal F_{b'})$ be transversely parallelizable foliations on compact connected manifolds, and assume that all basic functions on $(L_b,\mathcal F_b)$ and $(L_{b'},\mathcal F_{b'})$ are constant. Let $\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}}\in\Omega^1\bigl(L_b,l(L_b,\mathcal F_b)\bigr)$ and $\omega^{b'}_{\mathrm{MC}}\in\Omega^1\bigl(L_{b'},l(L_{b'},\mathcal F_{b'})\bigr)$ be the canonical Maurer--Cartan forms. If $\psi:(L_b,\mathcal F_b)\to(L_{b'},\mathcal F_{b'})$ is a foliated diffeomorphism, then
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $\psi_*$ induces a Lie algebra isomorphism $\psi':l(L_b,\mathcal F_b)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }l(L_{b'},\mathcal F_{b'})$, $\psi'(\bar Y)=\overline{\psi_*Y}$, where $Y\in L(L_b,\mathcal F_b)$ is a projectable vector field representing $\bar Y\in l(L_b,\mathcal F_b)$.
\item $\psi^*(\omega^{b'}_{\mathrm{MC}})=\psi'\circ\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
(i) Since $\psi$ is foliated, $d\psi$ sends $T(\mathcal F_b)$ into $T(\mathcal F_{b'})$, hence $\psi_*$ sends $\mathfrak X(\mathcal F_b)$ into $\mathfrak X(\mathcal F_{b'})$. Let $Y\in L(L_b,\mathcal F_b)$ be projectable. For any $X'\in\mathfrak X(\mathcal F_{b'})$, let $X:=(\psi^{-1})_*X'\in\mathfrak X(\mathcal F_b)$. Then
\[
[X',\psi_*Y]=[\psi_*X,\psi_*Y]=\psi_*[X,Y]\in \psi_*\mathfrak X(\mathcal F_b)\subseteq \mathfrak X(\mathcal F_{b'}),
\]
so $\psi_*Y\in L(L_{b'},\mathcal F_{b'})$. Therefore $\psi_*$ induces a map $\psi'\colon l(L_b,\mathcal F_b)\to l(L_{b'},\mathcal F_{b'})$ by passing to the quotient, $\psi'(\bar Y):=\overline{\psi_*Y}$.

It is a Lie algebra homomorphism because $\psi_*$ preserves Lie brackets. Its inverse is induced by $(\psi^{-1})_*$, hence $\psi'$ is a Lie algebra isomorphism.

(ii) Let $N(\mathcal F_b):=T(L_b)/T(\mathcal F_b)$ and $N(\mathcal F_{b'}):=T(L_{b'})/T(\mathcal F_{b'})$ be the normal bundles, with projections $\operatorname{pr}^N\colon T(L_b)\to N(\mathcal F_b)$ and $\operatorname{pr}^{N'}\colon T(L_{b'})\to N(\mathcal F_{b'})$.

Since $\psi$ is foliated, $d\psi$ induces $(d\psi)^N_x\colon N_x(\mathcal F_b)\to N_{\psi(x)}(\mathcal F_{b'})$ by $(d\psi)^N_x([v]):=[d\psi_x(v)]$. For $x\in L_b$, let $\mathrm{ev}_x\colon l(L_b,\mathcal F_b)\to N_x(\mathcal F_b)$, $\bar Y\mapsto \bar Y_x$, be the evaluation map, and similarly $\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}$ for $(L_{b'},\mathcal F_{b'})$. Under our hypotheses, these are linear isomorphisms, and the canonical Maurer--Cartan forms are $(\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)=\mathrm{ev}_x^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{pr}^N_x(\xi)\bigr)$, $(\omega^{b'}_{\mathrm{MC}})_{\psi(x)}(\zeta)=\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}^{-1}\bigl((\operatorname{pr}^{N'})_{\psi(x)}(\zeta)\bigr)$.

We claim that for all $x\in L_b$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ev-commutes-fixed}
\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}\circ \psi'=(d\psi)^N_x\circ \mathrm{ev}_x.
\end{equation}
Take $\bar Y\in l(L_b,\mathcal F_b)$ represented by a projectable $Y$. Then
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}(\psi'(\bar Y))
&=\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}(\overline{\psi_*Y})
=[(\psi_*Y)_{\psi(x)}]
=[d\psi_x(Y_x)]
=(d\psi)^N_x([Y_x])
=(d\psi)^N_x(\mathrm{ev}_x(\bar Y)),
\end{align*}
which proves \eqref{eq:ev-commutes-fixed}. Since $\mathrm{ev}_x$ and $\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}$ are isomorphisms, it follows that $\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}^{-1}\circ (d\psi)^N_x=\psi'\circ \mathrm{ev}_x^{-1}$.

Now let $\xi\in T_x(L_b)$. Because $\psi$ is foliated, $(\operatorname{pr}^{N'})_{\psi(x)}(d\psi_x(\xi))=(d\psi)^N_x(\operatorname{pr}^N_x(\xi))$. Therefore,
\begin{align*}
(\psi^*\omega^{b'}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)
&=(\omega^{b'}_{\mathrm{MC}})_{\psi(x)}(d\psi_x(\xi))\\
&=\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}^{-1}\bigl((\operatorname{pr}^{N'})_{\psi(x)}(d\psi_x(\xi))\bigr)\\
&=\mathrm{ev}_{\psi(x)}^{-1}\bigl((d\psi)^N_x(\operatorname{pr}^N_x(\xi))\bigr)\\
&=\psi'\left(\mathrm{ev}_x^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{pr}^N_x(\xi)\bigr)\right)\\
&=\psi'\bigl((\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr),
\end{align*}
which is $\psi^*(\omega^{b'}_{\mathrm{MC}})=\psi'\circ\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}}$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:alpha-sigma}
Let $X:=OF(M,\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal{F}:=\widetilde{\mathcal O}$, let $\kappa:X\to B$ be the fibre bundle of Theorem~\ref{thm:mol}, identified with the basic fibre bundle $\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}:X\to W$ via Corollary~\ref{cor:B-W-identification}, and let $A:=b(X,\mathcal{F})\to B$ be the basic Lie algebroid under this identification. Since $M$ and $O(q)$ are compact, $X$ is compact; as $B$ is a Hausdorff manifold, $\kappa$ is proper, so Lemma~\ref{lem:descend-to-B} applies to the maps induced by local bisections, which are foliated for $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:molino-data-invariant} and hence send leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}$ to leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{\pi^{-1}(V)}$.

Let $\sigma:U\to\mathcal{G}$ be a local bisection, let $V:=t(\sigma(U))$, and let $f_\sigma$ be the induced map on $OF(M,\mathcal O)$, with descended diffeomorphism $\bar f_\sigma:B_U\to B_V$ satisfying $\kappa\circ f_\sigma=\bar f_\sigma\circ\kappa$ on $\kappa^{-1}(B_U)$. For $b\in B_U$, write $b':=\bar f_\sigma(b)$ and $f_{\sigma,b}:=f_\sigma|_{L_b}:L_b\to L_{b'}$, and define
\[
\alpha_{\sigma,b}
:=
\operatorname{res}_{b'}^{-1}
\circ
(f_{\sigma,b})_*
\circ
\operatorname{res}_b
:
(\ker\rho_A)_b\longrightarrow(\ker\rho_A)_{b'}.
\]
Then each $\alpha_{\sigma,b}$ is a Lie algebra isomorphism, and these maps assemble into a smooth Lie algebra bundle isomorphism
\[
\alpha_\sigma:(\ker\rho_A)|_{B_U}\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }(\ker\rho_A)|_{B_V}
\]
covering $\bar f_\sigma$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Since $f_\sigma$ preserves $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$ and sends $L_b$ to $L_{b'}$, the restriction $f_{\sigma,b}:L_b\to L_{b'}$ is a foliated diffeomorphism from $(L_b,\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{L_b})$ to $(L_{b'},\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{L_{b'}})$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:MC-naturality}(i), it induces an isomorphism of structural Lie algebras
\[
(f_{\sigma,b})_*:
 l(L_b,\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{L_b})\to
 l(L_{b'},\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{L_{b'}}).
\]
Composing with the restriction isomorphisms of Lemma~\ref{lem:isotropy-structural-clean} gives the Lie algebra isomorphism $\alpha_{\sigma,b}$.

We now check smoothness. Let $\mathcal{W}\subseteq B_U$ be open and let $\zeta$ be a smooth local section of $\ker\rho_A$ over $\mathcal{W}$. By the construction of $A$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:basic-Lie-algebroid}, write $\zeta=\sum_i f_i\,e_i$ with $f_i\in C^\infty(\mathcal{W})$ in the trivialization $A\cong W\times \mathbb R^r$ determined by the transverse parallelism $\{\bar Y_1,\dots,\bar Y_r\}$; then the projectable vector field $Y:=\sum_i (f_i\circ\pi_{\operatorname{bas}})\,Y_i$ on $\kappa^{-1}(\mathcal{W})$, where $Y_i\in L(X,\mathcal{F})$ is the chosen projectable representative of $\bar Y_i$, represents $\zeta$. Since $\zeta$ takes values in $\ker\rho_A$, the definition of the anchor gives
\[
d\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}(Y)=\rho_A(\zeta)\circ\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}=0.
\]
After identifying $B$ and $W$, this is $d\kappa(Y)=0$. Since $f_\sigma$ is a foliated diffeomorphism, $(f_\sigma)_*Y$ is again projectable. Moreover, since
\[
\kappa\circ f_\sigma=\bar f_\sigma\circ \kappa,
\]
we have
\[
d\kappa((f_\sigma)_*Y)
=
d\bar f_\sigma(d\kappa(Y))=0.
\]
Therefore $(f_\sigma)_*Y$ represents a smooth local section of $\ker\rho_A$ over $\bar f_\sigma(\mathcal{W})$, and its value at $b'=\bar f_\sigma(b)$ is
\[
\operatorname{res}_{b'}^{-1}\Bigl(\,\overline{\bigl((f_\sigma)_*Y\bigr)\big|_{L_{b'}}}\,\Bigr)
=
\operatorname{res}_{b'}^{-1}\Bigl((f_{\sigma,b})_*\bigl(\,\overline{Y|_{L_b}}\,\bigr)\Bigr)
=
\alpha_{\sigma,b}\bigl(\zeta(b)\bigr).
\]
Hence $\alpha_\sigma$ sends smooth local sections to smooth local sections, so it is a smooth bundle map covering $\bar f_\sigma$ which is fibrewise a Lie algebra isomorphism. Applying the same construction to the inverse bisection $\sigma^{-1}$ yields the inverse bundle map, which is smooth by the same argument. Therefore $\alpha_\sigma$ is a smooth Lie algebra bundle isomorphism.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:vertical-MC}
In the situation of Lemma~\ref{lem:alpha-sigma}, for $b\in B$ write $L_b:=\kappa^{-1}(b)$, and let $\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}}$ denote the canonical Maurer--Cartan form of the Lie foliation $(L_b,\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})$, valued in $l(L_b,\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There exists a unique smooth section
\[
\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}} \in \Gamma\bigl((\ker d\kappa)^*\otimes \kappa^*(\ker\rho_A)\bigr)
\]
such that, for every $b\in B$, every $x\in L_b$, and every $\xi\in T_xL_b=\ker(d\kappa)_x$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:MC-res}
\operatorname{res}_b \bigl((\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr)=(\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi).
\end{equation}
\item The form $\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}}$ is equivariant under local bisections: for every local bisection $\sigma:U\to\mathcal{G}$, every $b\in B_U$, every $x\in L_b$, and every $\xi\in T_xL_b$,
\[
(\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_{f_\sigma(x)}\bigl((df_\sigma)_x\xi\bigr)
=
\alpha_{\sigma,b}\bigl((\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr).
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Recall that $X$ is compact, since $M$ and $O(q)$ are, and that $(X,\mathcal{F})$ is transversely parallelizable (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta-omega-parallelism}).

(i) For $x\in X$, let $b:=\kappa(x)$. By the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:isotropy-structural-clean}, evaluation at $x$ induces a linear isomorphism $\operatorname{ev}_x^X:A_b\longrightarrow N_x(\mathcal{F})$, $[\bar Y]\longmapsto \bar Y_x$, and, under this identification, the anchor $\rho_{A,b}:A_b\to T_bB$ corresponds to the map induced by $d\kappa:N_x(\mathcal{F})\longrightarrow T_bB$. Using local frames of $A$ coming from a transverse parallelism, these fibrewise maps assemble to a smooth vector bundle isomorphism $\operatorname{ev}^X:\kappa^*A\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }N(\mathcal{F})$, which identifies $\kappa^*(\ker\rho_A)$ with $\ker\bigl(d\kappa:N(\mathcal{F})\to \kappa^*(TB)\bigr)$.

Since $T(\mathcal{F})\subseteq \ker d\kappa$, the quotient map $TX\to N(\mathcal{F})=TX/T(\mathcal{F})$ restricts to
\[
q:\ker d\kappa\longrightarrow \ker\bigl(d\kappa:N(\mathcal{F})\to \kappa^*(TB)\bigr).
\]
Define
\[
\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}}:=\bigl(\operatorname{ev}^X|_{\kappa^*(\ker\rho_A)}\bigr)^{-1}\circ q.
\]
So at $x\in X$, if $\xi\in \ker(d\kappa)_x$, then $(\omega_{\mathrm{MC}}^{\kappa})_x(\xi)\in (\ker\rho_A)_b$. Because $q$ is smooth and $\operatorname{ev}^X|_{\kappa^*(\ker\rho_A)}$ is a smooth vector bundle isomorphism, the composition is smooth. So we have a smooth section of $(\ker d\kappa)^*\otimes \kappa^*(\ker\rho_A)$.

Now let $b\in B$, write $L_b=\kappa^{-1}(b)$, and note that, since $\kappa$ is constant on $L_b$, the pullback coefficient bundle restricts to the trivial bundle
\[
\kappa^*(\ker \rho_A)|_{L_b}\cong L_b\times (\ker \rho_A)_b,
\]
hence $\omega_{\mathrm{MC}}^{\kappa}|_{L_b}$ is a $(\ker \rho_A)_b$-valued $1$-form on $L_b$.

For $x\in L_b$, let $\operatorname{ev}_x^{L_b}:l(L_b,\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})\longrightarrow N_x(\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})$ be the evaluation isomorphism. By Lemma~\ref{lem:isotropy-structural-clean}, $(L_b,\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})$ is a Lie foliation and $\operatorname{res}_b:(\ker\rho_A)_b\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }l(L_b,\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})$ is a Lie algebra isomorphism. Moreover, we have shown that $\operatorname{ev}_x^{L_b}\circ \operatorname{res}_b = \operatorname{ev}_x^X\big|_{(\ker\rho_A)_b}$.

For $\xi\in T_xL_b=\ker(d\kappa)_x$, let $\bar\xi$ denote the class of $\xi$ in $N_x(\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})=T_xL_b/T_x(\mathcal{F})$. Then, by construction, $\operatorname{ev}_x^X((\omega_{\mathrm{MC}}^{\kappa})_x(\xi))=q_x(\xi)$, and under the identification $\ker\bigl(d\kappa:N_x(\mathcal{F})\to T_bB\bigr)\cong N_x(\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})$ this is $\bar\xi$. Hence $\operatorname{ev}_x^{L_b}(\operatorname{res}_b((\omega_{\mathrm{MC}}^{\kappa})_x(\xi)))=\bar\xi$.

Since $\operatorname{ev}_x^{L_b}$ is an isomorphism, it follows that
\[
\operatorname{res}_b \bigl((\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr)=(\operatorname{ev}_x^{L_b})^{-1}(\bar\xi).
\]
This is the formula for the Maurer--Cartan form of the Lie foliation $(L_b,\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})$, so \eqref{eq:MC-res} holds.

Uniqueness is immediate: since each $\operatorname{res}_b$ is an isomorphism, \eqref{eq:MC-res} determines the value $(\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)$ for every $x\in X$ and every $\xi\in\ker(d\kappa)_x$.

(ii) Since $f_{\sigma,b}:L_b\to L_{b'}$ is a foliated diffeomorphism (Lemma~\ref{lem:alpha-sigma}), we have $f_\sigma(x)\in L_{b'}$ and $(df_\sigma)_x\xi\in T_{f_\sigma(x)}L_{b'}=\ker(d\kappa)_{f_\sigma(x)}$. We first observe that both sides of the asserted identity lie in $(\ker\rho_A)_{b'}$: since $\kappa(f_\sigma(x))=\bar f_\sigma(\kappa(x))=b'$, the coefficient fibre $\bigl(\kappa^*(\ker\rho_A)\bigr)_{f_\sigma(x)}$ is $(\ker\rho_A)_{b'}$, so the left-hand side lies in $(\ker\rho_A)_{b'}$; the right-hand side does as well, since $\alpha_{\sigma,b}$ takes values in $(\ker\rho_A)_{b'}$.

Applying $\operatorname{res}_{b'}$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{res}_{b'}\Bigl((\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_{f_\sigma(x)}
  \bigl((df_\sigma)_x\xi\bigr)\Bigr)
&=(\omega^{b'}_{\mathrm{MC}})_{f_\sigma(x)}
  \bigl((df_\sigma)_x\xi\bigr)\\
&=(f_{\sigma,b})_*\bigl((\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr)\\
&=(f_{\sigma,b})_*\operatorname{res}_b
  \bigl((\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr)\\
&=\operatorname{res}_{b'}\Bigl(\alpha_{\sigma,b}
  \bigl((\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr)\Bigr).
\end{align*}
The first and third equalities use \eqref{eq:MC-res} on $L_{b'}$ and $L_b$, respectively. The second uses Lemma~\ref{lem:MC-naturality}(ii), applied to $f_{\sigma,b}$; its hypotheses hold as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:isotropy-structural-clean}. The last equality follows from the definition of $\alpha_{\sigma,b}$. Since $\operatorname{res}_{b'}$ is injective, the equivariance identity follows.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
We want to emphasize what Proposition~\ref{prop:vertical-MC} says conceptually.

A priori, each fibre $L_b$ carries its own Maurer--Cartan form, valued in the structural Lie algebra identified with $(\ker \rho_A)_b$; these are separate pieces of data on separate fibres. Proposition~\ref{prop:vertical-MC} says that the fibrewise Lie foliations are not isolated. Their Maurer--Cartan forms fit together into one global object $\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}}$, uniquely determined by \eqref{eq:MC-res}; the coefficient bundle of that global object is the pullback $\kappa^*(\ker \rho_A)$, and the whole object transforms equivariantly under the maps induced by local bisections of $\mathcal{G}$. Here the term Maurer--Cartan is meant fibrewise: for every $b\in B$, the $l(L_b,\mathcal{F}|_{L_b})$-valued form $\operatorname{res}_b\circ\omega^\kappa_{\mathrm{MC}}|_{L_b}$ is $\omega^b_{\mathrm{MC}}$ and satisfies the ordinary Maurer--Cartan equation on $L_b$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:Lie-algebroid-of-groupoid}
Let $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{inv}}^s(\mathcal{G})$ be the space of right-invariant source-vertical vector fields on $\mathcal{G}$,
\[
\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{inv}}^s(\mathcal{G}):=\{X\in \mathfrak X(\mathcal{G})\mid X_g\in \ker(ds)_g\quad \forall g\in \mathcal{G},\ X_{hg}=dR_g(X_h)\quad \forall (h,g)\text{ composable}\}.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{inv}}^s(\mathcal{G})$ is a Lie subalgebra of $\mathfrak X(\mathcal{G})$.

\item Restriction to the units identifies $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{inv}}^s(\mathcal{G})$ with $\Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
For $a\in\Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})$, its right-invariant extension is $(a^r)_g:=dR_g(a_{t(g)})$, and restriction to the units is inverse to $a\mapsto a^r$.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
Under the identification $\Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})\cong \mathfrak X_{\mathrm{inv}}^s(\mathcal{G})$, the bracket on $\Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})$ is induced from the Lie bracket of right-invariant source-vertical vector fields. More precisely, if $a,b\in \Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})$ with right-invariant extensions $a^r,b^r$, then
\[
[a,b]^r=[a^r,b^r].
\]

The anchor is induced by the derivative of the target map:
\[
\rho_{\mathcal{G}}:A_{\mathcal{G}}\to TM,\qquad \rho_{\mathcal{G}}(\xi)=dt(\xi).
\]
Equivalently, if $a\in \Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})$ and $a^r$ is its right-invariant extension, then $a^r$ is $t$-projectable to $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)$, that is, $dt(a^r)=\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)\circ t$.

Moreover, for $a,b\in \Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})$ and $f\in C^\infty(M)$, the Leibniz rule is
\[
[a,fb]=f[a,b]+\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)(f)b.
\]
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
The bracket part is immediate from the preceding discussion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

For the anchor, define $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}:A_{\mathcal{G}}\to TM$ by $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(\xi)=dt(\xi)$. Take $X\in \mathfrak X_{\mathrm{inv}}^s(\mathcal{G})$, and let $g:x\to y$. Since $g=1_yg$, we have $X_g=dR_g(X_{1_y})$. We then compute
\begin{align*}
    dt(X_g)=dt(dR_g(X_{1_y}))&=d(t\circ R_g)(X_{1_y})\\
    &=dt(X_{1_y}),
\end{align*}
because for any $h\in s^{-1}(y)$, $t(R_g(h))=t(hg)=t(h)$. We note that the right-hand side only depends on $y=t(g)$. Therefore $X$ is $t$-projectable. If we define $Y\in \mathfrak X(M)$ by $Y_y:=dt(X_{1_y})$, then $dt(X_g)=Y_{t(g)}$ for all $g\in \mathcal{G}$.

Now let $a\in \Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})$ and let $a^r$ be its right-invariant extension. By construction, $(a^r)_{1_x}=a_x$ for all $x\in M$, so the vector field $Y$ above is exactly $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)$. Hence $a^r$ is $t$-projectable to $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)$, that is, $dt(a^r)=\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)\circ t$.

Next we discuss the Leibniz rule. Let $a,b\in \Gamma(A_{\mathcal{G}})$ and $f\in C^\infty(M)$. We compute
\begin{align*}
    [a,fb]^r&=[a^r,(fb)^r]\\
    &=[a^r,(f\circ t)b^r]\quad\text{since }(fb)^r=(f\circ t)b^r\\
    &=(f\circ t)[a^r,b^r]+a^r(f\circ t)b^r\\
    &=(f\circ t)[a^r,b^r]+(\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)(f)\circ t)b^r\quad\text{because }a^r\text{ projects to }\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)\\
    &=(f[a,b])^r+(\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)(f)b)^r.
\end{align*}
Since the right-invariant extension map is injective, we conclude $[a,fb]=f[a,b]+\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)(f)b$.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
Since $a^r$ and $b^r$ are $t$-related to $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)$ and $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(b)$, the anchor is automatically a Lie algebra homomorphism: $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}([a,b])=[\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a),\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(b)]$. At this point we have the full Lie algebroid structure attached to the groupoid: $(A_{\mathcal{G}})_x=\ker(ds)_{1_x}$, $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}=dt|_{A_{\mathcal{G}}}$, with bracket induced from right-invariant source-vertical vector fields. When $\mathcal{G}$ is a Lie group, this right-invariant bracket on $T_e\mathcal{G}$ is the negative of the usual bracket defined by left-invariant vector fields.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:LieG-recovers-orbit}
Let $\mathcal{G}\rightrightarrows M$ be a regular Lie groupoid, let $A_{\mathcal{G}}=\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G})\to M$ be its Lie algebroid, and let $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}:A_{\mathcal{G}}\to TM$ be the anchor. For each $x\in M$, let $O_x$ be the orbit through $x$ and let $\mathcal{G}_x:=s^{-1}(x)\cap t^{-1}(x)$ be the isotropy group at $x$. Then $\operatorname{Im}(\rho_{\mathcal{G},x})=T_x(O_x)$ and $(\ker\rho_{\mathcal{G}})_x=\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G}_x)$. Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{Im}(\rho_{\mathcal{G}})=T(\mathcal O),
\]
and there is a short exact sequence of vector bundles
\[
0\longrightarrow \ker \rho_{\mathcal{G}}\longrightarrow A_{\mathcal{G}}\xrightarrow{\rho_{\mathcal{G}}} T(\mathcal O)\longrightarrow 0.
\]
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
We first show that the anchor recovers the orbit directions. Let $x\in M$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:orbit-submersion}, the restriction $t_x:=t|_{s^{-1}(x)}:s^{-1}(x)\to O_x$ is a surjective submersion. Differentiating at the unit $1_x$, and using $(A_{\mathcal{G}})_x=T_{1_x}(s^{-1}(x))=\ker(ds)_{1_x}$, we get $d(t_x)_{1_x}:(A_{\mathcal{G}})_x\to T_x(O_x)$. But $d(t_x)_{1_x}=dt_{1_x}|_{\ker(ds)_{1_x}}=\rho_{\mathcal{G},x}$ since $t_x$ is the restriction of $t$. Hence $\operatorname{Im}(\rho_{\mathcal{G},x})=T_x(O_x)$.

Since $\mathcal{G}$ is regular, the orbit foliation $\mathcal O$ has locally constant rank, so these spaces fit together into the tangent bundle $T(\mathcal O)\subseteq TM$. Thus $\operatorname{Im}(\rho_{\mathcal{G}})=T(\mathcal O)$.

Next we compute the isotropy of $A_{\mathcal{G}}$. The isotropy group at $x$ is $\mathcal{G}_x=s^{-1}(x)\cap t^{-1}(x)$. Its tangent space at the unit is
\[
T_{1_x}\mathcal{G}_x=T_{1_x}(s^{-1}(x)\cap t^{-1}(x))=\ker(ds)_{1_x}\cap \ker(dt)_{1_x}.
\]
But $(A_{\mathcal{G}})_x=\ker(ds)_{1_x}$ and $\rho_{\mathcal{G},x}=dt_{1_x}|_{\ker(ds)_{1_x}}$. Hence
\[
(\ker\rho_{\mathcal{G}})_x=\ker(ds)_{1_x}\cap \ker(dt)_{1_x}=T_{1_x}\mathcal{G}_x=\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G}_x).
\]

Since $\operatorname{Im}(\rho_{\mathcal{G}})=T(\mathcal O)$ is a vector subbundle of $TM$, the anchor has locally constant rank. Therefore we obtain the exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow \ker \rho_{\mathcal{G}}\longrightarrow A_{\mathcal{G}}\xrightarrow{\rho_{\mathcal{G}}} T(\mathcal O)\longrightarrow 0.
\]
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:ehresmann-connection}
Let $\mathcal{G}\rightrightarrows M$ be a Lie groupoid with $M$ Hausdorff. If $\mathcal{G}$ admits a smooth Riemannian metric, then it admits an Ehresmann connection $\Sigma:s^*TM\longrightarrow T\mathcal{G}$ satisfying $ds\circ\Sigma=\operatorname{id}_{s^*TM}$ and $\Sigma_{1_x}=(du)_x$ for every $x\in M$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Let $\eta^{(1)}$ be a Riemannian metric on $\mathcal{G}$. The orthogonal complement $(\ker ds)^{\perp_{\eta^{(1)}}}$ determines a smooth right splitting $\Sigma:s^*TM\longrightarrow T\mathcal{G}$ satisfying $ds\circ\Sigma=\operatorname{id}_{s^*TM}$. At the units, since $ds_{1_x}\circ du_x=\operatorname{id}_{T_xM}$,
\[
du_x-\Sigma_{1_x}:T_xM\longrightarrow A_{\mathcal{G},x}
\]
defines a smooth section of $\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{pr}_1^*TM,\operatorname{pr}_2^*A_{\mathcal{G}})\longrightarrow M\times M$ along the diagonal. Since $M$ is Hausdorff, the diagonal is closed. By \cite{Lee:ISM}*{Lemma~10.12}, there is a global smooth section $C$ satisfying $C(x,x)=du_x-\Sigma_{1_x}$. For $g\in\mathcal{G}$ and $v\in T_{s(g)}M$, replace $\Sigma$ by the smooth bundle map
\[
(g,v)\longmapsto\Sigma_g(v) +(dR_g)_{1_{t(g)}}\bigl(C(s(g),t(g))(v)\bigr).
\]
Note that the latter term lies in $\ker ds_g$, so this map remains a right splitting of $ds$. At the units, $\Sigma_{1_x}+C(x,x)=du_x$. Thus $\Sigma$ is an Ehresmann connection following \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Definition~2.8}.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{prop:normal-adjoint-cohomology}
Let $\mathcal{G}\rightrightarrows M$ be a regular Lie groupoid whose arrow manifold admits a Riemannian metric, let $A_{\mathcal{G}}:=\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G})$ be its Lie algebroid with anchor $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}:A_{\mathcal{G}}\to TM$, let $\mathcal O$ be the orbit foliation, and set $N:=TM/T\mathcal O$. For the adjoint representation up to homotopy
\[
\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})=\bigl(A_{\mathcal{G}}\xrightarrow{\rho_{\mathcal{G}}}TM\bigr),
\]
the induced representation on the degree-one cohomology bundle is canonically the normal representation $\lambda^N:\mathcal{G}\curvearrowright N$.

Equivalently, under the canonical identification $H^1(\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})) \cong TM/\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(A_{\mathcal{G}})=TM/T\mathcal O=N$, the degree-one cohomology representation of $\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})$ is $\lambda^N$.
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:ehresmann-connection}, choose an Ehresmann connection $\Sigma:s^*TM\longrightarrow T\mathcal G, ds\circ\Sigma=\operatorname{id}_{s^*TM}$, $\Sigma_{1_x}=(du)_x$ for every $x\in M$. Recall the construction of the adjoint representation up to homotopy from \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}. The adjoint complex of $\mathcal{G}$ is $\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})=\bigl(A_{\mathcal{G}}\xrightarrow{\rho_{\mathcal{G}}}TM\bigr)$, with $A_{\mathcal{G}}$ in degree $0$ and $TM$ in degree $1$ \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Definition~3.13}. The connection $\Sigma$ determines quasi-actions of $\mathcal{G}$ on $TM$ and on $A_{\mathcal{G}}$, both denoted $\lambda^\Sigma$, together with a basic curvature
\[
K^{\mathrm{bas}}_{\Sigma}\in\Gamma\bigl(\mathcal{G}^{(2)};\operatorname{Hom}(s^*TM,t^*A_{\mathcal{G}})\bigr).
\]
Let $r_g=(dR_g)_{1_{t(g)}}:A_{\mathcal G,t(g)}\to\ker(ds)_g$.
We use the following sign convention for the basic curvature:
\[
K^{\mathrm{bas}}_\Sigma(g,h)(v)=r_{gh}^{-1}\Bigl(dm_{g,h}\bigl(\Sigma_g(\lambda_h^\Sigma(v)),\Sigma_h(v)\bigr)-\Sigma_{gh}(v)\Bigr), \qquad v\in T_{s(h)}M,
\]
for composable arrows $g,h$. The quasi-action on $TM$ is given by \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Definition~2.11}:
\[
\lambda_g^\Sigma(v)=dt_g\bigl(\Sigma_g(v)\bigr),\qquad v\in T_{s(g)}M.
\]
The structure operators
\[
R_0=\rho_{\mathcal{G}},\qquad R_1=\lambda^\Sigma,\qquad R_2=K^{\mathrm{bas}}_{\Sigma}
\]
give $\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})$ the structure of a unital representation up to homotopy, denoted $\operatorname{Ad}_\Sigma(\mathcal{G})$ \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Proposition~3.14}, and the resulting object is independent of $\Sigma$ up to canonical isomorphism \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Proposition~3.16}. Among the structure equations \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Proposition~2.15}, we use the anchor equivariance
\begin{equation}\label{eq:anchor-equivariance}
\rho_{\mathcal{G}}\bigl(\lambda^\Sigma_g(a)\bigr)=\lambda^\Sigma_g\bigl(\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)\bigr),
\qquad a\in A_{\mathcal{G},s(g)},
\end{equation}
and the composition identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:basic-curvature-defect}
\lambda^\Sigma_g\lambda^\Sigma_h(v)-\lambda^\Sigma_{gh}(v)=\rho_{\mathcal{G}}\bigl(K^{\mathrm{bas}}_{\Sigma}(g,h)(v)\bigr),
\qquad v\in T_{s(h)}M,
\end{equation}
for composable arrows $g,h$ with $s(g)=t(h)$, so that the product is $gh$.

Since $\mathcal{G}$ is regular, the anchor has locally constant rank and its image is the orbit distribution: $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(A_{\mathcal{G}})=T\mathcal O$. Hence the complex of $\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})$ is regular in the sense of \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Definition~3.31}, and its degree-one cohomology bundle is
\[
H^1(\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G}))=TM/\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(A_{\mathcal{G}})=TM/T\mathcal O=N.
\]
By \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Theorem~3.32}, the quasi-action $\lambda^\Sigma$ induces an ordinary representation of $\mathcal{G}$ on $H^1(\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G}))\cong N$, the degree-one cohomology representation of $\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})$. We verify this directly from the structure equations and identify the resulting representation with the canonical normal representation.

Define $\lambda_g([v]):=[\lambda_g^\Sigma(v)]\in N_{t(g)}$ for $[v]\in N_{s(g)}$. This is well defined: if $v,v'\in T_{s(g)}M$ represent the same class, then $v-v'\in T_{s(g)}\mathcal O=\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(A_{\mathcal{G},s(g)})$, so $v-v'=\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)$ for some $a\in A_{\mathcal{G},s(g)}$, and by \eqref{eq:anchor-equivariance},
\[
\lambda^\Sigma_g(v)-\lambda^\Sigma_g(v')=\lambda^\Sigma_g\bigl(\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a)\bigr)=\rho_{\mathcal{G}}\bigl(\lambda^\Sigma_g(a)\bigr)\in T_{t(g)}\mathcal O.
\]
It is multiplicative: for composable arrows $g,h$, the identity \eqref{eq:basic-curvature-defect} gives $\lambda^\Sigma_g\lambda^\Sigma_h(v)-\lambda^\Sigma_{gh}(v)\in\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(A_{\mathcal{G}})=T\mathcal O$, so $\lambda_g\lambda_h=\lambda_{gh}$ on $N$.

The induced map on $N$ is independent of the connection: if $\Sigma'$ is another Ehresmann connection, then $\Sigma_g(v)-\Sigma'_g(v)\in\ker(ds_g)$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:orbit-submersion}, $dt_g(\ker ds_g)=T_{t(g)}\mathcal O$, so $[\lambda_g^\Sigma(v)]=[\lambda_g^{\Sigma'}(v)]$ in $N_{t(g)}$.

Finally, we identify the induced representation with $\lambda^N$. Let $g:x\to y$ and let $v\in T_xM$. Choose any $Y\in T_g\mathcal{G}$ such that $ds_g(Y)=v$. Then $Y-\Sigma_g(v)\in\ker(ds_g)$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:orbit-submersion} again,
\[
[dt_g(Y)]=[dt_g(\Sigma_g(v))]=[\lambda_g^\Sigma(v)]\qquad\text{in }N_y.
\]
By Definition~\ref{def:normal-orbit} and Proposition~\ref{prop:normal-global}, the class $[dt_g(Y)]$ is $\lambda_g^N([v])$. Thus $[\lambda_g^\Sigma(v)] = \lambda_g^N([v])$, and since Proposition~\ref{prop:normal-global} shows that $\lambda^N:\mathcal{G}\curvearrowright N$ is a smooth representation, the degree-one cohomology representation of $\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})$ is the canonical normal representation $\lambda^N$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{prop:lifted-action-groupoid-Lie-algebroid}
For the lifted action groupoid
\[
\mathcal{H}:=\mathcal{G}\ltimes OF(M,\mathcal O)\rightrightarrows OF(M,\mathcal O),
\]
there is a canonical Lie algebroid isomorphism
\[
\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{H})\cong \pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}},
\]
where $\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}$ is endowed with the action Lie algebroid structure induced by the infinitesimal lifted action of $A_{\mathcal{G}}$ on $OF(M,\mathcal O)$.
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
We use the convention described in Proposition~\ref{prop:Lie-algebroid-of-groupoid} and the subsequent discussion: the Lie algebroid of a Lie groupoid is defined using right-invariant source-vertical vector fields, with anchor induced by the target map.

For the corresponding action groupoid/action algebroid identification, see \cite{AriasAbadCrainic:RepUpToHomotopyGroupoids}*{Sec.~2.1}.

The arrow manifold of the lifted action groupoid is $\mathcal{G}\times_M OF(M,\mathcal O)$, with source and target maps $s_{\mathcal{H}}(g,e)=e$ and $t_{\mathcal{H}}(g,e)=g\cdot e$.

Fix $e\in OF(M,\mathcal O)$, and put $x=\pi(e)$. The unit arrow at $e$ is $u_{\mathcal{H}}(e)=(1_x,e)$. A tangent vector to $\mathcal{H}_1$ at $(1_x,e)$ is a pair $(a,\xi)\in T_{1_x}\mathcal{G}\oplus T_eOF(M,\mathcal O)$ satisfying $(ds)_{1_x}(a)=d\pi_e(\xi)$. Since $s_{\mathcal{H}}(g,e)=e$, one has $(ds_{\mathcal{H}})_{(1_x,e)}(a,\xi)=\xi$. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{H})_e=\ker(ds_{\mathcal{H}})_{(1_x,e)}=\{(a,0_e):a\in\ker(ds)_{1_x}\}.
\]
Since $(A_{\mathcal{G}})_x=\ker(ds)_{1_x}$, the fibrewise maps $(A_{\mathcal{G}})_{\pi(e)}\to\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{H})_e$, $a\mapsto(a,0_e)$, assemble into a canonical vector bundle isomorphism $\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}\cong\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{H})$.

Under this identification, let $a\in(A_{\mathcal{G}})_x$ and choose a smooth curve $g(\tau)$ in $s^{-1}(x)$ such that $g(0)=1_x$ and $g'(0)=a$. Then $\tau\mapsto(g(\tau),e)$ is a curve in $\mathcal{H}_1$ through $(1_x,e)$ whose derivative at $\tau=0$ is $(a,0_e)$. Hence the anchor sends $(a,0_e)$ to
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\right|_{\tau=0}g(\tau)\cdot e.
\]
This is the value at $e$ of the infinitesimal lifted action of $a$. Moreover, since $\pi(g(\tau)\cdot e)=t(g(\tau))$, differentiating at $\tau=0$ gives
\[
d\pi_e\left(\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\right|_{\tau=0}g(\tau)\cdot e\right)=(dt)_{1_x}(a)=\rho_{\mathcal{G}}(a).
\]
Thus the infinitesimal lifted action projects to the anchor of $A_{\mathcal{G}}$.

It remains to identify the bracket. Let $a$ be a local section of $A_{\mathcal{G}}$. Under the vector bundle identification above, the pullback section $\pi^*a$ corresponds to $e\mapsto(a_{\pi(e)},0_e)$. Let $a^r$ denote the right-invariant source-vertical vector field on $\mathcal{G}$ associated to $a$. For an arrow $(g,e)\in\mathcal{H}_1$, right multiplication by $(g,e)$ is the map $R_{(g,e)}:s_{\mathcal{H}}^{-1}(g\cdot e)\to s_{\mathcal{H}}^{-1}(e)$ given by $R_{(g,e)}(h,g\cdot e)=(hg,e)$. Under the same identification, the value of $\pi^*a$ at the target object $g\cdot e$ is $(a_{t(g)},0_{g\cdot e})$, and
\[
(dR_{(g,e)})_{(1_{t(g)},g\cdot e)}(a_{t(g)},0_{g\cdot e})=((a^r)_g,0_e).
\]
Thus the right-invariant source-vertical vector field on $\mathcal{H}$ associated to $\pi^*a$ is $(a^r,0)$.

For local sections $a,b$ of $A_{\mathcal{G}}$, it follows that
\[
[(a^r,0),(b^r,0)]=([a^r,b^r],0)=([a,b]^r,0).
\]
Hence $[\pi^*a,\pi^*b]=\pi^*[a,b]_{A_{\mathcal{G}}}$. Since pullbacks of a local frame of $A_{\mathcal{G}}$ form a local frame of $\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}$, this identity, together with the anchor computed above and the Lie algebroid Leibniz rule, determines the bracket on all local sections of $\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}$.

Thus the Lie algebroid structure transported from $\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{H})$ to $\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}$ is exactly the action Lie algebroid structure induced by the infinitesimal lifted action. Hence $\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{H})\cong\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}$ as Lie algebroids.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:molino-groupoid}
Let $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M$ be a regular Lie groupoid with $M$ compact and connected, and let $\eta^{(0)}$ be a $0$-metric on $M$. Let $\mathcal O$ be the orbit foliation, let $N:=TM/T(\mathcal O)$, let $q:=\operatorname{rank} N$, let $A_{\mathcal{G}}:=\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G})$ with anchor $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}:A_{\mathcal{G}}\to TM$, and let $g^N$ be the quotient metric on $N$ induced by $\eta^{(0)}$. Let $\pi:OF(M,\mathcal O)\to M$ be the transverse orthonormal frame bundle of $(N,g^N)$, and let $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$ be the lifted foliation.

Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The orbit foliation $(M,\mathcal O)$ is a Riemannian foliation. Consequently, Molino's classical structures of Theorem~\ref{thm:mol} are available for it: the foliated manifold $\bigl(OF(M,\mathcal O),\widetilde{\mathcal O}\bigr)$ is transversely parallelizable, with transverse canonical form $\theta$ and transverse Levi-Civita connection form $\omega$; there exist a smooth manifold $B$ with a smooth right $O(q)$-action and an $O(q)$-equivariant fibre bundle $\kappa:OF(M,\mathcal O)\to B$ whose fibres $L_b:=\kappa^{-1}(b)$ are the closures of the leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$; and each restriction $\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{L_b}$ is a Lie foliation with dense holonomy group. Moreover, $\kappa$ is proper.

\item If $\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}:OF(M,\mathcal O)\to W$ is the basic fibre bundle of $\bigl(OF(M,\mathcal O),\widetilde{\mathcal O}\bigr)$, and if $A:=b(OF(M,\mathcal O),\widetilde{\mathcal O})\to W$ denotes the associated basic Lie algebroid, then there is a unique diffeomorphism $\Phi:B\xrightarrow{\cong}W$ such that $\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}=\Phi\circ\kappa$. Via $\Phi$, we regard $A$ as a transitive Lie algebroid over $B$, and restriction to the fibre induces a Lie algebra isomorphism
\[
(\ker\rho_A)_b \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ } l\bigl(L_b,\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{L_b}\bigr).
\]

                                                                  
\item The fibrewise Maurer--Cartan forms assemble into a unique global section
\[
\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}}
\in
\Gamma\bigl((\ker d\kappa)^*\otimes \kappa^*(\ker\rho_A)\bigr)
\]
such that, for every $b\in B$, every $x\in L_b$, and every $\xi\in T_xL_b$,
\[
\operatorname{res}_b\bigl((\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr)=(\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi),
\]
where $\omega^{b}_{\mathrm{MC}}$ is the Maurer--Cartan form of the Lie foliation $(L_b,\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{L_b})$ and $\operatorname{res}_b$ is the restriction isomorphism in \textup{(ii)}.

\item If the arrow manifold of $\mathcal{G}$ admits a Riemannian metric, then the normal representation $\lambda^N:\mathcal{G}\curvearrowright N$ is the degree-one cohomology representation of the adjoint representation up to homotopy
\[
\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})=\bigl(A_{\mathcal{G}}\xrightarrow{\rho_{\mathcal{G}}}TM\bigr).
\]
It lifts canonically to a smooth left action of $\mathcal{G}$ on $OF(M,\mathcal O)$ with moment map $\pi$, given by $g\cdot e=\lambda_g^N\circ e$, and this action commutes with the right $O(q)$-action. The associated action groupoid
\[
\mathcal{H}:=\mathcal{G}\ltimes OF(M,\mathcal O)\rightrightarrows OF(M,\mathcal O)
\]
is a Lie groupoid and satisfies $\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{H})\cong\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}$ and $t_{\mathcal{H}}^*\theta=s_{\mathcal{H}}^*\theta$, where $\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}$ is endowed with the action Lie algebroid structure induced by the lifted action.

\item For every local bisection $\sigma:U\to \mathcal{G}$, the induced map $f_\sigma:\pi^{-1}(U)\to\pi^{-1}(t(\sigma(U)))$, $f_\sigma(e):=\sigma(\pi(e))\cdot e$, preserves $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$, $\theta$, and $\omega$. It sends each $\kappa$-fibre contained in $\pi^{-1}(U)$ onto a $\kappa$-fibre, and hence descends to a local $O(q)$-equivariant diffeomorphism $\bar f_\sigma$ of $B$. For each $b$ in the domain of $\bar f_\sigma$, the map
\[
\alpha_{\sigma,b}:=\operatorname{res}_{\bar f_\sigma(b)}^{-1}\circ(f_\sigma|_{L_b})_*\circ \operatorname{res}_{b}:
(\ker\rho_A)_b\to(\ker\rho_A)_{\bar f_\sigma(b)}
\]
is a Lie algebra isomorphism, and these maps assemble into a smooth Lie algebra bundle isomorphism $\alpha_\sigma$ covering $\bar f_\sigma$. Moreover, for $x\in L_b$ and $\xi\in T_xL_b$,
\[
(\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_{f_\sigma(x)}\bigl((df_\sigma)_x\xi\bigr)
=
\alpha_{\sigma,b}\bigl((\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}})_x(\xi)\bigr).
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Let $g^M:=\eta^{(0)}$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:0-metric}, the normal representation acts by fibrewise isometries for the induced metric $g^N$ on $N$. Proposition~\ref{prop:RF} shows that $(M,\mathcal O)$ is a compact connected Riemannian foliation.

Definitions~\ref{def:OF}, \ref{def:lifted-foliation}, and \ref{def:theta-omega} produce the transverse orthonormal frame bundle $\pi:OF(M,\mathcal O)\to M$, the lifted foliation $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$, the transverse canonical form $\theta$, the transverse Levi-Civita connection $\nabla^{\mathrm{tr}}$ on $N$, and the associated principal connection form $\omega$. Proposition~\ref{prop:transverse-LC-local} shows that $\omega$ is well-defined, vanishes on $T(\widetilde{\mathcal O})$, and is invariant under vector fields tangent to $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$; Lemma~\ref{lem:theta-omega-parallelism} yields the transverse parallelism of $\bigl(OF(M,\mathcal O),\widetilde{\mathcal O}\bigr)$.

Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:mol} to the compact connected Riemannian foliation $(M,\mathcal O)$ gives the smooth manifold $B$, the smooth right $O(q)$-action, and the $O(q)$-equivariant fibre bundle $\kappa:OF(M,\mathcal O)\to B$ whose fibres are the closures of the leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$. Since $M$ and $O(q)$ are compact, the total space $OF(M,\mathcal O)$ is compact; as $B$ is a Hausdorff manifold, $\kappa$ is proper. In particular, $\kappa$ satisfies the properness hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:descend-to-B}.

Let $X:=OF(M,\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal{F}:=\widetilde{\mathcal O}$. As observed in \cite{MoerdijkMrcun:IFLG}*{proof of Theorem~4.26}, $(X,\mathcal{F})$ is homogeneous. Since $X$ is compact and $(X,\mathcal{F})$ is transversely parallelizable, Proposition~\ref{prop:basic-Lie-algebroid} gives the transitive basic Lie algebroid $A:=b(X,\mathcal{F})\to W:=X/\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{bas}}$. Corollary~\ref{cor:B-W-identification} gives the unique diffeomorphism $\Phi:B\xrightarrow{\cong}W$ such that $\pi_{\operatorname{bas}}=\Phi\circ\kappa$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:isotropy-structural-clean} identifies $(\ker\rho_A)_b$ with $l(L_b,\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{L_b})$.

The unique global section $\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}}$ formed by the fibrewise Maurer--Cartan forms, together with its defining property \eqref{eq:MC-res}, is given by Proposition~\ref{prop:vertical-MC}(i). The identification of the normal representation with the degree-one cohomology representation of $\operatorname{Ad}(\mathcal{G})$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:normal-adjoint-cohomology}.

Proposition~\ref{prop:action-axioms} gives the smooth left action of $\mathcal{G}$ on $OF(M,\mathcal O)$, $g\cdot e=\lambda_g^N\circ e$, shows that it commutes with the right $O(q)$-action, and gives its canonical uniqueness property. Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-action-groupoid-Lie-algebroid} identifies the Lie algebroid of the lifted action groupoid $\mathcal{H}$ with the action Lie algebroid on the pullback bundle $\pi^*A_{\mathcal{G}}$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-action-groupoid} proves $t_{\mathcal{H}}^*\theta=s_{\mathcal{H}}^*\theta$.

Finally, let $\sigma:U\to \mathcal{G}$ be a local bisection, and let $V:=t(\sigma(U))$. Proposition~\ref{prop:molino-data-invariant} shows that the induced map $f_\sigma$ preserves $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$, $\theta$, and $\omega$; in particular, $f_\sigma$ is foliated for $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$ and sends leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}$ to leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}|_{\pi^{-1}(V)}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:descend-to-B} then gives the descended local diffeomorphism $\bar f_\sigma$ of $B$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:bisection-pseudogroup} gives compatibility with products, inverses, and the right $O(q)$-action. Lemma~\ref{lem:alpha-sigma} gives the smooth Lie algebra bundle isomorphism $\alpha_\sigma$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:vertical-MC}(ii) gives the equivariance formula for $\omega^{\kappa}_{\mathrm{MC}}$.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
The basic Lie algebroid $A\to W$ and the Lie algebroid $A_{\mathcal{G}}\to M$ fit into the exact sequences
\[
0\longrightarrow \ker \rho_A\longrightarrow A\xrightarrow{\rho_A}TW\longrightarrow 0
\]
and
\[
0\longrightarrow \ker \rho_{\mathcal{G}}\longrightarrow A_{\mathcal{G}}\xrightarrow{\rho_{\mathcal{G}}} T(\mathcal O)\longrightarrow 0.
\]

So $\rho_{\mathcal{G}}$ gives the leaf/orbit directions on $M$, while $\rho_A$ gives directions on the closure base $W$. The isotropy $(\ker\rho_{\mathcal{G}})_x=\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal{G}_x)$ is the pointwise isotropy Lie algebra of the original groupoid, while $(\ker\rho_A)_w$, equivalently $(\ker\rho_A)_b$ after identifying $B\cong W$, is the structural Lie algebra of the Lie foliation on the closure fibre $L_b$.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:bibundle-pullback-groupoid}
Let $\mathcal{G}'\curvearrowright P\curvearrowleft\mathcal{G}$ be a Morita equivalence bibundle with moment maps $\alpha':P\to M'$ and $\alpha:P\to M$. Let $\mathcal K_P\rightrightarrows P$ be the pullback groupoid of $\mathcal{G}$ through $\alpha$: its arrows are the triples $(p_1,g,p_0)$ with $s(g)=\alpha(p_0)$ and $t(g)=\alpha(p_1)$, with source $p_0$, target $p_1$, and multiplication $(p_2,h,p_1)(p_1,g,p_0)=(p_2,hg,p_0)$. Then:

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item $z:\mathcal K_P\to\mathcal{G}$, $(p_1,g,p_0)\mapsto g$, is a Morita fibration with object map $\alpha$.
\item For each arrow $(p_1,g,p_0)$ of $\mathcal K_P$ there is a unique $g'\in\mathcal{G}'$ with $p_1\cdot g=g'\cdot p_0$, and $z':\mathcal K_P\to\mathcal{G}'$, $(p_1,g,p_0)\mapsto g'$, is a Morita fibration with object map $\alpha'$.
\item For $p\in P$, the maps $g'\mapsto g'\cdot p$ and $g\mapsto p\cdot g$ are diffeomorphisms
\[
s_{\mathcal{G}'}^{-1}(\alpha'(p))\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\alpha^{-1}(\alpha(p)),
\qquad
t_{\mathcal{G}}^{-1}(\alpha(p))\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }(\alpha')^{-1}(\alpha'(p)).
\]
In particular, if $\mathcal{G}'$ and $\mathcal{G}$ have connected source fibres, then $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ have connected fibres.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Both moment maps are surjective submersions, since $\alpha'$ is the bundle projection of the principal right $\mathcal{G}$-action and $\alpha$ that of the principal left $\mathcal{G}'$-action. Hence $\mathcal K_P$ is a Lie groupoid.

(1) By construction, the square formed by $z$ and the maps $(s,t)$ is a pullback, so $z$ is fully faithful. Since its object map is $\alpha$, it is a Morita fibration.

(2) For an arrow $(p_1,g,p_0)$, we have $\alpha(p_1\cdot g)=s(g)=\alpha(p_0)$. Principality of the left $\mathcal{G}'$-action gives a unique $g'\in\mathcal{G}'$ with $p_1\cdot g=g'\cdot p_0$, depending smoothly on $(p_1,g,p_0)$ through the smooth inverse of the principal map. Moreover, $s(g')=\alpha'(p_0)$ and $t(g')=\alpha'(p_1)$. If $p_2\cdot h=h'\cdot p_1$, then, because the two actions commute,
\[
p_2\cdot(hg)=(p_2\cdot h)\cdot g
=h'\cdot(p_1\cdot g)=(h'g')\cdot p_0,
\]
so $z'$ preserves multiplication; by uniqueness it preserves units and inverses.

Conversely, for an arrow $(p_1,g',p_0)$ in the pullback groupoid of $\mathcal{G}'$ through $\alpha'$, principality of the right $\mathcal{G}$-action gives a unique $g$ with $p_1\cdot g=g'\cdot p_0$, depending smoothly on the data. Thus $(p_1,g,p_0)\mapsto(p_1,g',p_0)$ is an isomorphism of Lie groupoids over $P$ from $\mathcal K_P$ to this pullback groupoid. Under this identification, $z'$ is the projection to $\mathcal{G}'$, hence a Morita fibration since $\alpha'$ is a surjective submersion.

(3) Principality of the left action over $M$ says that $(g',p)\mapsto(g'\cdot p,p)$ is a diffeomorphism $\mathcal{G}'\times_{M'}P\to P\times_MP$; restricting to the fibre over $p$ gives the first diffeomorphism. The second follows in the same way from principality of the right action over $M'$. Since inversion identifies $t_{\mathcal{G}}^{-1}(\alpha(p))$ with $s_{\mathcal{G}}^{-1}(\alpha(p))$, we are done.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:lifted-frame-groupoid-properties}
The lifted frame groupoid $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}\rightrightarrows OF(T)$ is Hausdorff, proper, free, and \'{e}tale.

Therefore the orbit space $B_{\mathcal{E}}:=OF(T)/\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ has a unique smooth manifold structure such that the quotient map $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}:OF(T)\to B_{\mathcal{E}}$ is a surjective local diffeomorphism. Its fibre through $u\in OF(T)$ is the $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$-orbit
\[
\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}(\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u))=\widehat{\mathcal{E}}\cdot u=\{d_{\pi_T(u)}\psi_g\circ u : g\in\mathcal{E}_1, s(g)=\pi_T(u)\}.
\]
Moreover, the right $O(q)$-action on $OF(T)$ descends to a smooth right $O(q)$-action on $B_{\mathcal{E}}$, defined by $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)\cdot A:=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(uA)$.
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
We first show that $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is \textit{\'{e}tale}. The source map $\widehat s$ is the pullback of the local diffeomorphism $s:\mathcal{E}_1\to T$ along $\pi_T$, hence is a local diffeomorphism. Since inversion is a diffeomorphism, $\widehat t$ is also a local diffeomorphism, so $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is \'etale.

We next show \textit{properness}. Let $K\subseteq OF(T)\times OF(T)$ be compact. Since $\mathcal{E}$ is proper, $(s,t)^{-1}((\pi_T\times\pi_T)(K))$ is compact, and $\operatorname{pr}_1(K)$ is compact. The set
\[
D:=\{(g,u)\in (s,t)^{-1}((\pi_T\times\pi_T)(K)) \times \operatorname{pr}_1(K):s(g)=\pi_T(u)\}
\]
is closed in $(s,t)^{-1}((\pi_T\times\pi_T)(K)) \times \operatorname{pr}_1(K)$, hence compact. The map $D\to OF(T)\times OF(T)$, $(g,u)\mapsto (u,d_{\pi_T(u)}\psi_g\circ u)$, is continuous, and the inverse image of $K$ is $(\widehat s,\widehat t)^{-1}(K)$. Hence $(\widehat s,\widehat t)^{-1}(K)$ is compact, so $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is proper.

We now show \textit{freeness}. Suppose $(g,u)$ fixes $u\in OF(T)_x$. Then $g\in\mathcal{E}_x$ and $d_x\psi_g\circ u=u$. Since $u$ is a linear isomorphism, $d_x\psi_g=\operatorname{id}_{T_xT}$.

The germ $\psi_g$ is represented by a local isometry fixing $x$ with $d_x\psi_g=\operatorname{id}_{T_xT}$. After shrinking this representative, choose $\epsilon>0$ such that $\exp_x:B(0,\epsilon)\subseteq T_xT\to W\subseteq T$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open neighbourhood of $x$ contained in the domain of this representative. By naturality of the exponential map under local isometries,
\[
\psi_g(\exp_x v)=\exp_x(d_x\psi_g(v))=\exp_x(v)
\]
for all $v\in B(0,\epsilon)$. Hence $\psi_g$ is the identity germ at $x$. Since $\mathcal{E}$ is effective, $g=1_x$. Therefore $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is free.

                                                                                                                     
Since $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ has trivial isotropy, the map $(\widehat s,\widehat t):\widehat{\mathcal{E}}_1\to OF(T)\times OF(T)$ is injective. Its target is Hausdorff. Hence $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}_1$ is Hausdorff.

We have shown that $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is proper, free, and \'{e}tale. Since $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is proper, the orbit space $B_{\mathcal{E}}=OF(T)/\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is Hausdorff. By \cite{HenriquesMetzler:NoneffectiveOrbifolds}*{Proposition~4.2 and Corollary~4.3}, $B_{\mathcal{E}}$ has a smooth manifold structure for which $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}:OF(T)\to B_{\mathcal{E}}$ is a surjective local diffeomorphism. This structure is the unique one with this property.

The fibre formula follows immediately from the definition of the orbit space. Finally, right translation by any $A\in O(q)$ sends $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$-orbits to $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$-orbits, so $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)\cdot A:=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(uA)$ defines a right $O(q)$-action on $B_{\mathcal{E}}$.

The composite of the descended action with $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\times\operatorname{id}_{O(q)}$ is the smooth map $(u,A)\mapsto\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(uA)$. Since $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\times\operatorname{id}_{O(q)}$ is a surjective local diffeomorphism, its local inverses show that the descended action is smooth.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- proposition-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:OF-P-Morita-bibundle}
Let $\mathcal{E}'\curvearrowright P\curvearrowleft \mathcal{E}$ be a Riemannian Morita equivalence bibundle as above. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item $\dim T=\dim P=\dim T'=:q$, and the moment maps $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ are surjective local isometries. They induce $O(q)$-equivariant surjective local diffeomorphisms of orthonormal frame bundles
\[
OF(\alpha):OF(P)\to OF(T),
\qquad
OF(\alpha)(\xi)=d_p\alpha\circ \xi,
\]
and
\[
OF(\alpha'):OF(P)\to OF(T'),
\qquad
OF(\alpha')(\xi)=d_p\alpha'\circ \xi,
\]
where $\xi\in OF_p(P)$.

\item The frame bundle $OF(P)$ is an $O(q)$-equivariant Morita bibundle $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}'\curvearrowright OF(P)\curvearrowleft \widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ between the lifted frame groupoids, with moment maps $OF(\alpha')$ and $OF(\alpha)$.

\item There is a unique $O(q)$-equivariant diffeomorphism $\Phi_P:B_{\mathcal{E}}\longrightarrow B_{\mathcal{E}'}$ such that
\[
\Phi_P\circ\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha)=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}\circ OF(\alpha')
\]
on $OF(P)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-20 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
(1) Since $\mathcal{E}$ and $\mathcal{E}'$ are \'etale, Lemma~\ref{lem:bibundle-pullback-groupoid}\textup{(3)} shows that $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ have discrete fibres. Both maps are submersions, so $\dim T=\dim P=\dim T'=:q$.

Because the bibundle is Riemannian, the maps $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ are Riemannian submersions. Since they are submersions between manifolds of equal dimension, they are local diffeomorphisms, hence local isometries. Therefore they induce the surjective local diffeomorphisms of orthonormal frame bundles. They are $O(q)$-equivariant:
\[
OF(\alpha)(\xi A)=d_p\alpha\circ\xi\circ A=OF(\alpha)(\xi)A, \qquad OF(\alpha')(\xi A)=OF(\alpha')(\xi)A.
\]

(2) We \textit{lift the right $\mathcal{E}$-action on $P$}. Let $(g,u)\in\widehat{\mathcal{E}}_1$, where $g:x\to y$ and $u\in OF_x(T)$, and let $\xi\in OF_p(P)$ satisfy $OF(\alpha)(\xi)=\widehat t(g,u)=d_x\psi_g\circ u$; in particular, $\alpha(p)=y=t(g)$, so the right action by $g$ is defined. Let $R_g$ be the germ of the local right action map on $P$ induced by a local bisection through $g$, so $R_g(p)=p\cdot g$. It satisfies $\alpha\circ R_g=\psi_{g^{-1}}\circ\alpha$ and $\alpha'\circ R_g=\alpha'$; differentiating the first identity at $p$ gives $d_{p\cdot g}\alpha\circ d_pR_g=d_y\psi_{g^{-1}}\circ d_p\alpha$. Define $\xi\cdot(g,u):=d_pR_g\circ\xi$. Then, as linear maps,
\[
d_{p\cdot g}\alpha\circ\bigl(\xi\cdot(g,u)\bigr)
=d_y\psi_{g^{-1}}\circ d_p\alpha\circ\xi
=d_y\psi_{g^{-1}}\circ d_x\psi_g\circ u
=u.
\]
Since $d_{p\cdot g}\alpha$ is a linear isometry and $u$ is an orthonormal frame, $\xi\cdot(g,u)=(d_{p\cdot g}\alpha)^{-1}\circ u$ is an orthonormal frame; thus $\xi\cdot(g,u)\in OF_{p\cdot g}(P)$ and $OF(\alpha)(\xi\cdot(g,u))=u$. Also, $OF(\alpha')(\xi\cdot(g,u))=d_{p\cdot g}\alpha'\circ d_pR_g\circ\xi=d_p\alpha'\circ\xi=OF(\alpha')(\xi)$, using $\alpha'\circ R_g=\alpha'$. So this defines a right action of $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ on $OF(P)$ with moment map $OF(\alpha)$.

Similarly, we \textit{lift the left $\mathcal{E}'$-action}. Let $(g',u')\in\widehat{\mathcal{E}}'_1$, where $g':x'\to y'$ and $u'\in OF_{x'}(T')$, and let $\xi\in OF_p(P)$ satisfy $OF(\alpha')(\xi)=u'$. Let $L_{g'}$ denote the germ of the local left action map, $L_{g'}(p)=g'\cdot p$; it satisfies $\alpha'\circ L_{g'}=\psi_{g'}\circ\alpha'$ and $\alpha\circ L_{g'}=\alpha$. Define $(g',u')\cdot\xi:=d_pL_{g'}\circ\xi$. By the same argument, $(g',u')\cdot\xi\in OF_{g'\cdot p}(P)$, with $OF(\alpha')\bigl((g',u')\cdot\xi\bigr)=d_{x'}\psi_{g'}\circ u'$ and $OF(\alpha)\bigl((g',u')\cdot\xi\bigr)=OF(\alpha)(\xi)$. So this defines a left action of $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}'$ on $OF(P)$ with moment map $OF(\alpha')$.

The \textit{two lifted actions commute} because the $\mathcal{E}'$- and $\mathcal{E}$-actions on $P$ commute, $g'\cdot(p\cdot g)=(g'\cdot p)\cdot g$: differentiating gives $dL_{g'}\circ dR_g=dR_g\circ dL_{g'}$, so $(g',u')\cdot\bigl(\xi\cdot(g,u)\bigr)=\bigl((g',u')\cdot\xi\bigr)\cdot(g,u)$. The associativity and unit identities follow in the same way from the corresponding identities for the original actions on $P$, and smoothness follows in local bisection charts.

Next we discuss \textit{principality}. Take frames $\xi_1\in OF_{p_1}(P)$ and $\xi_2\in OF_{p_2}(P)$ with $OF(\alpha')(\xi_1)=OF(\alpha')(\xi_2)$; then $\alpha'(p_1)=\alpha'(p_2)$. Since the right $\mathcal{E}$-action on $P$ is principal over $T'$, there is a unique arrow $g:x\to y$ in $\mathcal{E}$ such that $p_2=p_1\cdot g$. Since $\alpha'\circ R_g=\alpha'$, we get $d_{p_2}\alpha'\circ d_{p_1}R_g\circ\xi_1=d_{p_1}\alpha'\circ\xi_1=d_{p_2}\alpha'\circ\xi_2$. Because $d_{p_2}\alpha'$ is an isomorphism, $d_{p_1}R_g\circ\xi_1=\xi_2$. Applying $d_{p_2}\alpha$ and the differentiated identity above gives $OF(\alpha)(\xi_2)=d_y\psi_{g^{-1}}\circ OF(\alpha)(\xi_1)$, that is, $OF(\alpha)(\xi_1)=d_x\psi_g\circ OF(\alpha)(\xi_2)$; hence the lifted action is defined and $\xi_2=\xi_1\cdot\widehat g$ with $\widehat g:=(g,OF(\alpha)(\xi_2))$.

\textit{Uniqueness of $\widehat g$} follows from the uniqueness of $g$. The assignment $(\xi_1,\xi_2)\mapsto\widehat g$ is smooth, because $g$ is obtained from the smooth inverse of the principal map $P\times_T\mathcal{E}_1\to P\times_{T'}P$ and $OF(\alpha)(\xi_2)$ depends smoothly on $\xi_2$. Hence the lifted right $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$-action is principal.

For the left principality, the proof is symmetric: if $OF(\alpha)(\xi_1)=OF(\alpha)(\xi_2)$, then $\alpha(p_1)=\alpha(p_2)$, there is a unique arrow $g'$ in $\mathcal{E}'$ with $p_1=g'\cdot p_2$, and differentiating $\alpha\circ L_{g'}=\alpha$ gives $\xi_1=d_{p_2}L_{g'}\circ\xi_2=(g',u')\cdot\xi_2$ with $u':=OF(\alpha')(\xi_2)$. Therefore $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}'\curvearrowright OF(P)\curvearrowleft\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is a Morita bibundle.

Finally, we check \textit{$O(q)$-equivariance}. The right $O(q)$-action on each arrow manifold is $(g,u)A=(g,uA)$, and the moment maps $OF(\alpha)$ and $OF(\alpha')$ are $O(q)$-equivariant by part (1). For the lifted actions, $(\xi A)\cdot\bigl((g,u)A\bigr)=d_pR_g\circ\xi\circ A=\bigl(\xi\cdot(g,u)\bigr)A$, and similarly $\bigl((g',u')A\bigr)\cdot(\xi A)=\bigl((g',u')\cdot\xi\bigr)A$. Thus $OF(P)$ is an $O(q)$-equivariant Morita bibundle.

(3) Define $\Phi_P$ by requiring $\Phi_P\circ\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha) =\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}\circ OF(\alpha')$ on $OF(P)$. Since $OF(\alpha):OF(P)\to OF(T)$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}:OF(T)\to B_{\mathcal{E}}$ are surjective local diffeomorphisms, so is the composite $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha):OF(P)\to B_{\mathcal{E}}$; hence this requirement determines $\Phi_P$ uniquely once it is well-defined.

\begin{comment}
                                        
                                                       
                                                       
                                                      
                                              
                                    
                                 
  
                                 
                                   
  

                                                    
                                           
                                                        
                                                   
                                                     
                                         
                                                     
                                       
                                              
  
                                 
                                   
  

                                                                                                          
                                                        
                                                      
                

\end{comment}

Suppose $\xi_0,\xi_1\in OF(P)$ have the same image under $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha)$, and put $u_i:=OF(\alpha)(\xi_i)$ for $i=0,1$. Then $u_0,u_1$ lie in the same $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$-orbit, so there is an arrow $(g,u_1):u_1\to u_0$. The lifted right action therefore gives
\[
OF(\alpha)\bigl(\xi_0\cdot(g,u_1)\bigr)
=u_1=OF(\alpha)(\xi_1).
\]
By the left principality established in (2), there is an arrow of $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}'$ carrying $\xi_1$ to $\xi_0\cdot(g,u_1)$. Their $OF(\alpha')$-images therefore lie in the same $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}'$-orbit. Since the lifted right action preserves $OF(\alpha')$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}(OF(\alpha')(\xi_0))
&=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}\bigl(OF(\alpha')(\xi_0\cdot(g,u_1))\bigr)\\
&=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}(OF(\alpha')(\xi_1)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}\circ OF(\alpha')$ is constant on the fibres of $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha)$, and $\Phi_P$ is well-defined.


Using the lifted left action and right principality in the same way shows that $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha)$ is constant on the fibres of $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}\circ OF(\alpha')$. Hence the two composites have the same fibres. By part (1) and Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-frame-groupoid-properties}, both are surjective local diffeomorphisms onto Hausdorff manifolds. Therefore Lemma~\ref{lem:same-fibres-diffeo} shows that $\Phi_P:B_{\mathcal{E}}\to B_{\mathcal{E}'}$ is a diffeomorphism.

Finally, $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha)$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}\circ OF(\alpha')$ are $O(q)$-equivariant by part (1) and Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-frame-groupoid-properties}. The defining identity for $\Phi_P$ and the surjectivity of $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha)$ therefore show that $\Phi_P$ is $O(q)$-equivariant.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:etale-theta-omega-morita}
Let $\mathcal{E}\rightrightarrows T$ be a proper effective \'etale Riemannian groupoid, let $\theta_T\in\Omega^1(OF(T),\mathbb{R}^q)$ and $\omega_T\in\Omega^1(OF(T),\mathfrak o(q))$ be the canonical form and the Levi-Civita connection form of $\pi_T:OF(T)\to T$, and let $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}:OF(T)\to B_{\mathcal{E}}$ be the quotient map.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item On $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}_1$ we have $\widehat t^{\,*}\theta_T=\widehat s^{\,*}\theta_T$ and $\widehat t^{\,*}\omega_T=\widehat s^{\,*}\omega_T$. Consequently, there are unique forms $\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}\in\Omega^1(B_{\mathcal{E}},\mathbb{R}^q)$ and $\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}\in\Omega^1(B_{\mathcal{E}},\mathfrak o(q))$ with
\[
\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^*\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}=\theta_T,
\qquad
\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^*\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}=\omega_T,
\]
and for every $b\in B_{\mathcal{E}}$ the map $(\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}},\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}}})_b:T_bB_{\mathcal{E}}\to\mathbb{R}^q\oplus\mathfrak o(q)$ is a linear isomorphism.
\item In the situation of Proposition~\ref{prop:OF-P-Morita-bibundle}, let $\theta_{T'}$, $\theta_P$ and $\omega_{T'}$, $\omega_P$ be the canonical forms and the Levi-Civita connection forms of $OF(T')$ and $OF(P)$. Then
\[
OF(\alpha)^*\theta_T=\theta_P=OF(\alpha')^*\theta_{T'},
\qquad
OF(\alpha)^*\omega_T=\omega_P=OF(\alpha')^*\omega_{T'}
\]
on $OF(P)$, and $\Phi_P^*\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}'}}=\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}$, $\Phi_P^*\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}'}}=\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
(1) Let $g:x\to y$ be an arrow of $\mathcal{E}$, and choose a local $s$-bisection $\sigma:U\to\mathcal{E}$ through $g$, with $U$ so small that $h:=t\circ\sigma:U\to V$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset $V\subseteq T$. By \cite{MdHF-LieGpdMetrics}*{Lemma~3.1.5}, $h$ is a local isometry for the given $0$-metric on $T$, and its frame lift $OF(h):OF(T)|_U\to OF(T)|_V$, $OF(h)(u):=d_{\pi_T(u)}h\circ u$, satisfies $\pi_T\circ OF(h)=h\circ\pi_T$. The computation in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:functoriality-molino}, with $N=TT$ and $\operatorname{pr}^N=\operatorname{id}$, gives $OF(h)^*\theta_T=\theta_T$ on $OF(T)|_U$, and the naturality of the Levi-Civita connection under the local isometry $h$ \cite{Lee:IRM}*{Proposition~5.13} gives $OF(h)^*\omega_T=\omega_T$ on $OF(T)|_U$, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:functoriality-molino}.

Near $(g,u)$ the arrows of $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ are parametrized by $v\mapsto(\sigma(\pi_T(v)),v)$, $v\in OF(T)|_U$; in this chart $\widehat s$ is the identity and $\widehat t$ is $OF(h)$. Hence $\widehat t^{\,*}\theta_T=\widehat s^{\,*}\theta_T$ and $\widehat t^{\,*}\omega_T=\widehat s^{\,*}\omega_T$ near $(g,u)$, and such charts cover $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}_1$.

Since $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ is a surjective local diffeomorphism, the descended forms are unique if they exist. For $b\in B_{\mathcal{E}}$, $v\in T_bB_{\mathcal{E}}$, and $u\in\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}(b)$, put
\[
(\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}})_b(v):=(\theta_T)_u\bigl((d\kappa_{\mathcal{E}})_u^{-1}v\bigr),
\qquad
(\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}}})_b(v):=(\omega_T)_u\bigl((d\kappa_{\mathcal{E}})_u^{-1}v\bigr).
\]
If $u_0,u_1\in\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^{-1}(b)$, the fibre description of Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-frame-groupoid-properties} gives an arrow $g$ with $u_1=d_x\psi_g\circ u_0$. With $\sigma$ and $h$ as above, $OF(h)(u_0)=u_1$, and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(h)=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ on $OF(T)|_U$, because $OF(h)$ maps each frame into its $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$-orbit. Differentiating gives $(d\kappa_{\mathcal{E}})_{u_1}^{-1}v=dOF(h)_{u_0}\bigl((d\kappa_{\mathcal{E}})_{u_0}^{-1}v\bigr)$, and the invariance of $\theta_T$ and $\omega_T$ under $OF(h)$ shows that the two definitions do not depend on $u$. On an open set $W\subseteq OF(T)$ on which $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset, the descended forms are $((\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}|_W)^{-1})^*\theta_T$ and $((\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}|_W)^{-1})^*\omega_T$, hence smooth, and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^*\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}=\theta_T$, $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^*\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}=\omega_T$.

Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:theta-omega-parallelism}, applied to the foliation of $T$ by points, shows that $(\theta_T,\omega_T)_u$ is a linear isomorphism for every $u\in OF(T)$. Since $(d\kappa_{\mathcal{E}})_u$ is an isomorphism, the pullback identities above imply the same for $(\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}},\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}}})_{\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)}$.

(2) By Proposition~\ref{prop:OF-P-Morita-bibundle}\textup{(1)}, the maps $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ are local isometries. The calculation for the canonical form and the naturality of the Levi-Civita connection in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:functoriality-molino} therefore apply locally and give
\[
OF(\alpha)^*\theta_T=\theta_P=OF(\alpha')^*\theta_{T'},
\qquad
OF(\alpha)^*\omega_T=\omega_P=OF(\alpha')^*\omega_{T'}.
\]

For the last part, Proposition~\ref{prop:OF-P-Morita-bibundle}(3) gives $\Phi_P\circ\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha)=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}'}\circ OF(\alpha')$. Hence
\[
(\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha))^*\Phi_P^*
\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}'}}
=\theta_P
=(\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha))^*
\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}.
\]
Since $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}\circ OF(\alpha)$ is a surjective local diffeomorphism, pullback of forms along it is injective, so $\Phi_P^*\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}'}}=\theta_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}$. The same argument gives $\Phi_P^*\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}'}}=\omega_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:molino-proper-etale}
Let $\mathcal{E}\rightrightarrows T$ be a proper effective \'etale Riemannian groupoid, and let $B_{\mathcal{E}}=OF(T)/\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ with its descended right $O(q)$-action.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item The map $B_{\mathcal{E}}/O(q)\to T/\mathcal{E}$, $[\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)]\mapsto[\pi_T(u)]$, is a homeomorphism.

\item For $u\in OF_x(T)$, the map $\mathcal{E}_x\to O(q)$, $g\mapsto u^{-1}\circ d_x\psi_g\circ u$, is an injective group homomorphism whose image is the stabilizer of $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)$ in $O(q)$. In particular, all stabilizers of the descended $O(q)$-action are finite.

\item $OF(T)$ is a Morita equivalence bibundle $\mathcal{E}\curvearrowright OF(T)\curvearrowleft\bigl(B_{\mathcal{E}}\rtimes O(q)\bigr)$ with moment maps $\pi_T$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ and actions $g\cdot u=d_{\pi_T(u)}\psi_g\circ u$ and $u\cdot(b,A)=uA$ for $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)=b$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ is Morita equivalent to $B_{\mathcal{E}}\rtimes O(q)$; compare \cite{HenriquesMetzler:NoneffectiveOrbifolds}*{Prop.~5.2}.

\item If $\mathcal{E}'\rightrightarrows T'$ is a proper effective \'etale Riemannian groupoid and $\mathcal{E}'\curvearrowright P\curvearrowleft\mathcal{E}$ is a Riemannian Morita equivalence bibundle, then the $O(q)$-equivariant diffeomorphism $\Phi_P:B_{\mathcal{E}}\to B_{\mathcal{E}'}$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:OF-P-Morita-bibundle} induces a Lie groupoid isomorphism
\[
B_{\mathcal{E}}\rtimes O(q)\longrightarrow B_{\mathcal{E}'}\rtimes O(q),
\qquad b\longmapsto\Phi_P(b), \quad (b,A)\longmapsto(\Phi_P(b),A).
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
(1) If $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(v)$, then $v=d_{\pi_T(u)}\psi_g\circ u$ for an arrow $g:\pi_T(u)\to\pi_T(v)$, so $\pi_T(u)$ and $\pi_T(v)$ have the same class in $T/\mathcal{E}$; also $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)A=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(uA)$ and $\pi_T(uA)=\pi_T(u)$. Hence the map is well-defined, and it is surjective because every point of $T$ admits an orthonormal frame. If $[\pi_T(u)]=[\pi_T(v)]$, choose an arrow $g:\pi_T(u)\to\pi_T(v)$; the frames $g\cdot u:=d_{\pi_T(u)}\psi_g\circ u$ and $v$ lie over the same point, so $v=(g\cdot u)A$ for a unique $A\in O(q)$, and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(v)=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)A$. Thus the map is injective.

The quotient map $T\to T/\mathcal{E}$ is open, because the saturation $t(s^{-1}(U))$ of an open subset $U\subseteq T$ is open; the quotient map $B_{\mathcal{E}}\to B_{\mathcal{E}}/O(q)$ is open, because the saturation of an open subset is the union of its right translates. Since $\pi_T$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ are open, the two composites $OF(T)\to T/\mathcal{E}$ and $OF(T)\to B_{\mathcal{E}}/O(q)$ are continuous open surjections, and the bijection just constructed identifies their fibres. Hence both spaces carry the quotient topology of $OF(T)$, and the bijection is a homeomorphism.

(2) Fix $u\in OF_x(T)$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-frame-groupoid-properties}, $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)A=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)$ if and only if $uA=d_x\psi_g\circ u$ for some arrow $g$ with $s(g)=x$; since $\pi_T(uA)=x$, such a $g$ lies in $\mathcal{E}_x$, and then $A=u^{-1}\circ d_x\psi_g\circ u$. The identity $d_x\psi_{hg}=d_x\psi_h\circ d_x\psi_g$ shows that $g\mapsto u^{-1}\circ d_x\psi_g\circ u$ is a group homomorphism, and its kernel is trivial because $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is free. Hence it identifies $\mathcal{E}_x$ with the stabilizer of $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)$. Finally, $\mathcal{E}_x$ is compact by properness and discrete by \'etaleness, hence finite.

(3) Both moment maps $\pi_T$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ are surjective submersions. The left action is the lifted action of Proposition~\ref{prop:action-axioms}; it satisfies $\pi_T(g\cdot u)=t(g)$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(g\cdot u)=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)$. The right action is smooth, and for $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)=b$ we have $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u\cdot(b,A)) =\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(uA)=bA=s(b,A)$, $\pi_T(uA)=\pi_T(u)$, $u\cdot(b,\operatorname{id})=u$, and $(u\cdot(b,A))\cdot(bA,C)=u(AC)$, so it is an action. The two actions commute because $g\cdot(uA)=(g\cdot u)A$.

The right action is principal over $T$: after eliminating the coordinate $b=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}(u)$, its principal map is
\[
OF(T)\times O(q)\longrightarrow OF(T)\times_T OF(T),
\qquad
(u,A)\longmapsto(uA,u),
\]
which is a diffeomorphism since $\pi_T:OF(T)\to T$ is a principal $O(q)$-bundle.

The left action is principal over $B_{\mathcal{E}}$: the map
\[
\mathcal{E}_1\times_T OF(T)
\longrightarrow OF(T)\times_{B_{\mathcal{E}}}OF(T),
\qquad
(g,u)\longmapsto(g\cdot u,u),
\]
is surjective because the fibres of $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ are the $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$-orbits, and injective because $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is free. The projection of the domain onto $u$ is $\widehat s$, a local diffeomorphism since $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}$ is \'etale. The projection of the codomain onto its second factor is the pullback of the local diffeomorphism $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ along $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$, hence a local diffeomorphism as well. The smooth principal map commutes with these projections, so it is a bijective local diffeomorphism, hence a diffeomorphism.

(4) By the $O(q)$-equivariance of $\Phi_P$, the maps in the statement define a Lie groupoid isomorphism. Its inverse is given by $\Phi_P^{-1}$ on objects and $(b',A)\mapsto(\Phi_P^{-1}(b'),A)$ on arrows.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:etale-compatible-2metric}
Let $\mathcal{E}\rightrightarrows T$ be a proper effective \'etale Riemannian groupoid. Then $B_{\mathcal{E}}\rtimes O(q)$ admits a $2$-metric $\eta'$ with the following property. If $\eta'^{(0)}$ denotes its induced $0$-metric on $B_{\mathcal{E}}$, then the metric $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^*\eta'^{(0)}$ on $OF(T)$ makes the bibundle of Corollary~\ref{cor:molino-proper-etale}\textup{(3)} a Riemannian Morita equivalence bibundle.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Let $\eta^{(0)}$ be the given $0$-metric on $T$, and let $\eta$ be its unique extension to a $2$-metric on $\mathcal{E}$.

We first verify that $\mathcal{E}_1$ is Hausdorff. Each germ $\psi_g$ is represented by a local isometry for $\eta^{(0)}$, so the map
\[
g\longmapsto
\bigl(s(g),t(g),d_{s(g)}\psi_g\bigr)
\]
takes values in the Hausdorff manifold of linear isometries between tangent spaces of $T$. Since $\mathcal{E}$ is \'etale, we have $d_{s(g)}\psi_g=dt_g\circ(ds_g)^{-1}$, so this map is smooth.

Suppose that $g,h:x\to y$ have the same image. Then
\[
d_x\psi_{h^{-1}g}
=(d_x\psi_h)^{-1}\circ d_x\psi_g
=\operatorname{id}_{T_xT}.
\]
The exponential map argument in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-frame-groupoid-properties} shows that $\psi_{h^{-1}g}$ is the identity germ. Since $\mathcal{E}$ is effective, $h^{-1}g=1_x$, hence $g=h$. Thus the map is injective. Disjoint open neighbourhoods of the images of two distinct arrows pull back to disjoint open neighbourhoods of the arrows, so $\mathcal{E}_1$ is Hausdorff.

Let $\mathcal K\rightrightarrows OF(T)$ be the pullback groupoid of $\mathcal{E}$ through $\pi_T$. Lemma~\ref{lem:bibundle-pullback-groupoid}, applied to the bibundle of Corollary~\ref{cor:molino-proper-etale}\textup{(3)}, gives Morita fibrations
\[
z:\mathcal K\longrightarrow\mathcal{E},
\qquad
z':\mathcal K\longrightarrow B_{\mathcal{E}}\rtimes O(q)
\]
with object maps $\pi_T$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$, respectively. The arrow manifold of $\mathcal K$ is a fibre product inside $OF(T)\times\mathcal{E}_1\times OF(T)$, and is therefore Hausdorff. The arrow manifold $B_{\mathcal{E}}\times O(q)$ is Hausdorff as well.

We next identify the normal spaces of the $\mathcal K$-orbits. By the definition of the pullback groupoid, for every $u\in OF(T)$,
\[
\mathcal K\cdot u
=
\pi_T^{-1}\bigl(\mathcal{E}\cdot\pi_T(u)\bigr).
\]
Since $\mathcal{E}$ is proper and \'etale, its orbits are discrete subsets of $T$, so $T_u(\mathcal K\cdot u)=\ker(d\pi_T)_u$. The differential of $\pi_T$ therefore identifies the normal space to the orbit at $u$ with $T_{\pi_T(u)}T$:
\[
T_uOF(T)/\ker(d\pi_T)_u
\longrightarrow T_{\pi_T(u)}T,
\qquad
[v]\longmapsto(d\pi_T)_u(v).
\]

By \cite{MdHFStackMetrics}*{Prop.~6.3.1}, there is a $2$-metric $\tilde\eta$ on $\mathcal K$ making $z$ a Riemannian submersion in the sense of \cite{MdHFStackMetrics}*{Definition~3.2.1}. In particular, $\pi_T:\bigl(OF(T),\tilde\eta^{(0)}\bigr)\longrightarrow\bigl(T,\eta^{(0)}\bigr)$ is a Riemannian submersion. Hence, for each $u\in OF(T)$, the map $[v]\mapsto(d\pi_T)_u(v)$ is an isometry for the metric induced by $\tilde\eta^{(0)}$ on the normal space and the metric $\eta^{(0)}$ on $T_{\pi_T(u)}T$.

Applying \cite{MdHFStackMetrics}*{Prop.~6.3.2 and the proof of Thm.~6.3.3} to $z'$ and $\tilde\eta$, we obtain a $2$-metric $\eta'$ on $B_{\mathcal{E}}\rtimes O(q)$ and a $2$-metric $\tilde\eta'$ on $\mathcal K$ making $z'$ a Riemannian submersion. Moreover, $\tilde\eta^{(0)}$ and $\tilde\eta'^{(0)}$ induce the same metric on the normal bundle of every $\mathcal K$-orbit. Hence, for every $u\in OF(T)$, the map $[v]\mapsto(d\pi_T)_u(v)$ remains an isometry for the metric induced by $\tilde\eta'^{(0)}$ and the given metric $\eta^{(0)}$. It follows from \cite{MdHF-LieGpdMetrics}*{Sec.~2.1} that $\pi_T:(OF(T),\tilde\eta'^{(0)})\to(T,\eta^{(0)})$ is a Riemannian submersion.

Finally, the object map $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ of $z'$ is a Riemannian submersion for $\tilde\eta'^{(0)}$ and $\eta'^{(0)}$. Since $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}$ is a local diffeomorphism, this means $\tilde\eta'^{(0)}=\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^*\eta'^{(0)}$. Both moment maps are therefore Riemannian submersions for the metric $\kappa_{\mathcal{E}}^*\eta'^{(0)}$, as required by Definition~\ref{def:morita-data-prelim}\textup{(iii)}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
\label{rem:no-effectiveness-regular}
We used \textit{effectiveness} only in the proper \'etale subsection, where it implies that the lifted frame groupoid $\widehat{\mathcal{E}}\rightrightarrows OF(T)$ is free (Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-frame-groupoid-properties}).

We did not use this hypothesis in Theorem~\ref{thm:molino-groupoid}. There we work directly with the full Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G}\rightrightarrows M$, local bisections, and the normal representation $\lambda^N$. Isotropy acting trivially on transverse directions is therefore retained as part of the groupoid data in the regular theory.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:frame-bundle-pullback}
Let $\phi:\bigl(\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}\rightrightarrows \widetilde M\bigr)\rightarrow \bigl(\mathcal{G}\rightrightarrows M\bigr)$ be a Morita fibration, and write \(\phi_0:=\phi^{(0)}:\widetilde M\to M\) and $\phi_1:=\phi^{(1)}:\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}\to\mathcal{G}$. Then $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}$ is regular if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ is regular. In this case the orbit foliations \(\mathcal O_{\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}}\) and \(\mathcal O\) satisfy $T\mathcal O_{\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}} = (d\phi_0)^{-1}(T\mathcal O)$, and \(d\phi_0\) descends to a vector bundle isomorphism
\[
\overline{d\phi_0}:\nu(\mathcal O_{\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}})
\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ } \phi_0^{*}\nu(\mathcal O),
\qquad
(\overline{d\phi_0})_{\tilde m}([v])
=[(d\phi_0)_{\tilde m}(v)].
\]
In particular, if $\mathcal O$ has constant codimension $q$, then so does $\mathcal O_{\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}}$.

Assume now that $\mathcal O$ has constant codimension $q$, and equip \(\widetilde M\) and \(M\) with Riemannian metrics for which \(\overline{d\phi_0}\) is fibrewise isometric for the induced metrics on the normal bundles; this holds whenever $\phi_0$ is a Riemannian submersion. Then there is a canonical \(O(q)\)-equivariant principal bundle isomorphism
\[
F_\phi: OF(\widetilde M,\mathcal O_{\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}}) \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ } \phi_0^{*}OF(M,\mathcal O),
\qquad
